name: Morningside and Florida Road
tagline: The city's social spine, restaurants and Victorian houses
description: The established inner suburb on the Berea ridge, built around Florida Road with its restored Victorian houses now holding the city's best concentration of restaurants, bars and coffee shops. It is where most of Durban's professional and international residents live.
bestFor: Almost anyone arriving, for the restaurants and the residential security
pros: The best restaurant and bar strip in Durban
Established residential streets with good security
Ten minutes from the beachfront by car
cons: Walking at night is not advisable
Load shedding affects the area like everywhere

name: Umhlanga
tagline: The northern beach town, newer, safer and more expensive
description: A separate coastal town fifteen kilometres north, developed over the last three decades into Durban's business and residential alternative, with a lighthouse, a promenade, secure apartment complexes and the Gateway shopping centre. It is the safest-feeling place in the metropolitan area and priced accordingly.
bestFor: Stays that prioritise security and a modern apartment over city character
pros: The safest-feeling area in greater Durban
Business district, malls and the airport road
cons: The highest rents in the metropolitan area
Car-dependent and short on street life
Twenty to thirty minutes into central Durban

name: Glenwood
tagline: The university suburb, students and old houses under trees
description: The residential suburb around the University of KwaZulu-Natal's Howard College campus, with older houses, mature trees, a student population and a growing run of cafes and small restaurants along Davenport Road. Rents are lower than Morningside and the character is more mixed.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting lower rents, trees and a student-adjacent neighbourhood
pros: Cafes and small restaurants along Davenport
University facilities and the botanic gardens nearby
cons: Property crime is a real and constant concern
Fifteen minutes from the beach by car

name: North Beach and the Golden Mile
tagline: The beachfront promenade, surf and the seaside strip
description: The long beachfront running north from the harbour, with a rebuilt promenade, the piers, reliable surf and the warmest sea water in South Africa. Hotels and older apartment blocks face it. It is the city's best public space by day and requires real caution after dark.
bestFor: Stays that want to surf and swim from the door, with caution accepted
pros: Warm ocean and reliable surf year-round
The rebuilt promenade for running and cycling
Cheaper apartments than the ridge suburbs
cons: Genuinely unsafe to walk after dark
Older, tired apartment blocks in parts
Busy and crowded on public holidays

name: Musgrave and Berea
tagline: The ridge above the city, older flats and good value
description: The residential ridge running along the top of the city with older apartment buildings, jacaranda streets, the Musgrave shopping centre and views down to the harbour. It is central, well served and cheaper than Morningside, with a mixed and long-settled population.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a central flat at a moderate rent
pros: Central position with views over the city and harbour
Rents below Morningside for similar space
Shops, clinics and services along the ridge
cons: Security concerns as elsewhere in the city
